title: Chicago PMI / Chicago Business Barometer (Dec 2026 data) — the year's final release
source: NEWS: mnimarkets.com "Chicago Business Barometer™ (aka Chicago PMI): 2025/26 Publication Calendar", re-fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200) — the 2026 schedule lists all twelve releases at 09:45 ET and reads "December 30" at "09:45", alongside the "September 30" entry this proposer's own event sits on and the "October 30"/"November 30" entries already on the calendar. Note the URL correction this fetch produced: the path the 08-29 and 09-05 rows cited (mnimarkets.com/chicago-business-barometer) now returns HTTP 404, and the live calendar is at /chicago-business-barometer-aka-chicago-pmi-publication-calendar — the source string above is the working one. Stays `estimate` on the same two structural counts every Chicago instance carries, neither of them date doubt: this lane never self-promotes an adjacency it proposed, and `market-events-data.ts`'s confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for MNI/ISM-Chicago at all (`ISM:` is scoped to ismworld.org's national PMI calendar), while the alternative publisher route stays closed — chicago.ismworld.org's report page 302s to ecommerce.ismworld.org/SSO/Login.aspx, re-tested this same session. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: DISCOVERED IN THE chicago-pmi-2026-09-30 D-15 ADJACENCY SWEEP (2026-09-15). Completes a coverage gap this series has been closing one instance at a time: every comparable recurring macro series here carries three or four forward entries (ISM Manufacturing 09-01/10-01/11-02/12-01, ISM Services, CPI, jobs, ADP, Beige Book), and Chicago carried one instance until 2026-09-05, then two, then three — 09-30, 10-30, 11-30 — and stopped, even though MNI's own calendar names a twelfth release. Two reasons it is worth carrying rather than left to be rediscovered. First, it is the only Chicagoland manufacturing read that lands AFTER the 2026-12-09 FOMC, so it is the first datapoint measured against a known year-end policy rate rather than against a live rate debate — the 11-30 instance's note records that it is one of the last prints the committee sees before that meeting, and this is the bookend to it. Second, it closes the 2026 series at a full twelve observations, which is what the parent ledger's own base-rate arithmetic runs on: that doc's mean-reversion call is graded off a trailing standard deviation (sigma 7.59 across 2026 vs 3.43 the prior year), and a dispersion statistic computed on eleven of twelve months is a worse statistic than one computed on all twelve. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and no tracked symbol carries direct Chicagoland manufacturing exposure; impact is tiered medium to match its three siblings, not because a December regional survey moves a tape. Estimate widens caution only and licenses no date-keyed action. Full ledger: docs/research/events/chicago-pmi-2026-09-30.md.
